title: Candidate feedback draft: Oliver Chen - Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
summary: Strong backend engineer with good systems instincts and fast iteration. Good fit for medium-complexity infra work but needs ramp on LLM-specific KV cache and attention optimization concepts. Recommended to move to take-home/onsite pairing to validate design tradeoffs.
high_level_takeaways: Very pragmatic, ships quickly, thoughtful about tradeoffs. Implemented similar caching and async processing in previous role. Missed some nuance on KV cache eviction strategies and quantized inference pitfalls - could be brought up to speed with a focused ramp. Communication is clear and concise.
strengths: Shipping velocity, pragmatic tradeoff reasoning, strong debugging and observability habits, good ownership traces in prior role.
weaknesses: Limited hands-on experience with transformer internals and quantization. Needs mentoring on platform-level kernel selection and low-level perf debugging. Some gaps in large-scale ASYNC batching design patterns.
overall_recommendation: Move forward to take-home assignment and on-site pairing. Not a strong hire as-is for senior infra role; good match for IC 2/3 with potential to grow into infra specialization.
recommended_next_steps: Send take-home exercise focused on designing a small KV cache + batching layer for a toy transformer host. If take-home shows expected approaches, schedule an onsite pair with Jordan for kernel selection and Priya for implementation review.
detailed_notes:
Screener: quick intro, behavioral signals strong (shipped telemetry and rollback flows).
Coding: implemented a streaming parser problem in ~40m, clean code, good test thinking but needed prompting on worst-case complexity and concurrency hazards.
System design: proposed a sharded cache + leaky-bucket batching approach; high level ok but didn't discuss cache eviction corner cases or hot-key skew mitigation in detail.
Culture/behavioral: good ownership examples, mentored juniors, focused on stability and rollback.
